identity.title: Alcohol use (CAGE) and time since last drink; tremor, diaphoresis, agitation (CIWA items)

technique.how: Ask the four CAGE questions (Cut down, Annoyed, Guilty, Eye-opener), quantity/frequency, and the exact time of the last drink. Score CIWA-Ar items at the bedside: nausea, tremor (arms extended), sweats, anxiety, agitation, tactile/auditory/visual disturbances, headache, orientation (0-67).
technique.prerequisites: Patient able to answer or a collateral historian; CIWA-Ar requires a communicative patient.
technique.contraindications: CIWA-Ar is unreliable in patients who cannot communicate (intubated, delirious from another cause, severe dementia).

interpretation.positive_finding: CAGE >=2 raises the probability of DSM alcohol abuse/dependence (pooled LR+ 3.44; sensitivity 0.87 in inpatients). Last drink 6-24 h ago with tremor/sweats/agitation fits early withdrawal; 48-96 h fits delirium tremens.
interpretation.negative_finding: CAGE <2 lowers but does not exclude an alcohol use disorder (pooled LR- 0.18; sensitivity only 0.60 in ambulatory patients). A drink within the last few hours makes withdrawal an unlikely cause of current symptoms.
interpretation.pitfalls: CAGE detects abuse/dependence, not hazardous drinking, and performs poorly in women, prenatal and primary-care populations. CIWA-Ar is a severity scale, not a diagnostic test, and is inflated by pain, sepsis, hypoglycemia and anxiety.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive: give thiamine before glucose, start symptom-triggered benzodiazepines, check glucose/ammonia. Negative: pursue other AMS causes; still consider Wernicke if malnourished.

estimates.target_condition: DSM-defined alcohol abuse or dependence; CAGE score >=2 (inpatients)
estimates.population: Hospital inpatients from studies pooled in a diagnostic meta-analysis (10 studies overall)
estimates.reference_standard: DSM criteria for alcohol abuse/dependence (structured interview)
estimates.quote: the pooled sensitivity is far better in inpatients (0.87) than in primary care patients (0.71) or ambulatory patients (0.60)

estimates.target_condition: DSM-defined alcohol abuse or dependence; CAGE score >=2 (primary care)
estimates.population: Primary care patients from pooled studies
estimates.quote: the pooled sensitivity is far better in inpatients (0.87) than in primary care patients (0.71) or ambulatory patients (0.60)

estimates.target_condition: DSM-defined alcohol abuse or dependence; CAGE score >=2 (all populations)
estimates.population: General clinical populations, 10 pooled studies (inpatient, primary care, ambulatory)
estimates.quote: The likelihood ratios seem to be relatively constant over the populations (overall LR+:3.44;LR-:0.18)

sources.citation: Aertgeerts B, Buntinx F, Kester A. The value of the CAGE in screening for alcohol abuse and alcohol dependence in general clinical populations: a diagnostic meta-analysis. J Clin Epidemiol. 2004;57(1):30-39.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use CIWA-Ar to drive sedation in patients who cannot communicate or whose agitation may be from another cause (sepsis, hypoxia, head injury, hypoglycemia).
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Seizure, fever, marked autonomic instability or hallucinations with confusion 48-96 h after the last drink suggest delirium tremens or Wernicke; give IV thiamine and escalate care.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: CIWA-Ar was designed for reliability and validity in monitored withdrawal (Sullivan 1989); CAGE test-retest reliability 0.80-0.95 (Dhalla 2007, PMID 17716538).

extraction_notes: Kitchens 1994 RCE has no abstract on PubMed and no PMC text, so its tables could not be viewed; it is cited as the anchor without numbers. CAGE numbers are from the Aertgeerts 2004 meta-analysis abstract (cutoff >=2): pooled sensitivity by setting and overall LR+/LR-; pooled specificities are stated to differ by group but are not given in the abstract, so specificity is null. No diagnostic-accuracy data were found for 'time since last drink' or for CIWA-Ar items as discriminators of withdrawal versus other AMS causes; CIWA-Ar (PMID 2597811) is a severity/monitoring scale, cited as consensus. Status partially_quantified.
